Health workers in Bunia, Ituri province — epicentre of DR Congo's deadliest-ever Ebola outbreak — began receiving the Ervebo vaccine on Saturday under a 70,000-dose compassionate-use campaign. The country has recorded 7,541 confirmed cases and 3,639 deaths, and the WHO warns the toll could surpass the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.

Elaine Mokhtefi, American witness to the Algerian Revolution, dies at 97

Elaine Mokhtefi, an American-born translator and activist who joined Algeria's National Liberation Front and lived in Algiers for 12 years after independence, died September 11 in New York at 97. She organized the 1969 Pan-African Cultural Festival and helped arrange Black Panther Eldridge Cleaver's exile in Algiers. Her 2018 memoir, Algiers, Third World Capital, chronicled her decades among revolutionaries from Frantz Fanon to Fidel Castro.

24Atrocities Watch Africa

Egypt’s Strategic Concerns in the Horn

Egypt reveres its position and role in the greater Middle East/Red Sea region. Since its shift from monarchy to republic in 1952, through the Free Officers Coup led by military leader and former President Gamal Abdel Nasser, its regional power largely situates itself in 1956 and the nationalization of the Suez Canal. Amid a backdrop of ongoing Arab Israeli wars, Sudan’s independence, the Yemen Civil war, and growing turbulence across the wider region, Egypt arguably established itself as the bedrock of the emerging regional security architecture, designed by the postcolonial rising United States imperial power.
